- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.1) and price is rising, model often underestimates; increase forecast slightly to match momentum.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak for next 3 periods.  
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, consider mean reversion; adjust downward by 1–3% if sentiment is neutral or negative.  
- When sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.5 → 0.1 → 0.5), model often fails to capture volatility; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast for next 2 periods.  
- If model forecast is below true outcome by >3% for 3+ consecutive days, model is underestimating; increase forecast by 1–2% for next period unless sentiment is strongly negative.
